scope: Independent semantic review of the inactive mutable source chain and alternative request/downstream adapters.

findings.finding: The new nine-body route obtains its A1 pair from `linkage_fixture_source`, whose two adapters are concretely specialized to `*const Element` (the source builder spells these types in the generated signatures and transmute substitutions). `insert_a1_pair` inserts those bytes unchanged, then requires that the combined source contain no `*const Element`; there is no mutable type rewrite or finite rewrite inventory for this component.
findings.impact: The actual pinned A1 pair cannot pass the new route's own post-insertion gate, so `write_case` cannot emit its advertised mutable nine-body candidate. The synthetic test supplies generic `Src`/`Dst` adapters without the pinned const-pointer signatures, so it misses this failure.
findings.fix: Add a separately pinned, finite type rewrite for the A1 component signatures/substitutions, verify exact mutable pointer depth and runtime/ghost-strip identity, and test against a synthetic pair that retains the actual `*const Element` source shapes.

findings.finding: The alternative `transform_pair`/`write_candidate` path rewrites and writes a source candidate but has no Cloud provider gate. It can be invoked locally despite CORE's Cloud-only actual-preparation boundary.
findings.impact: The new candidate adds a source-preparation entry point that can emit transformed full-unit source outside the assigned Cloud provider environment.
findings.fix: Apply the pinned Cloud-only provider gate before reading/writing this source candidate, or remove/limit the adapter so it cannot perform source preparation outside the authorized Cloud path.

findings.finding: `validate_pair` accepts an omitted `contract_text_sha256` by defaulting it to the expected constant, without hashing the contract bytes in `verified`. The output stage then records the expected contract hash unconditionally. A synthetic mutable pair with the helper's unwind contract changed to `on_unwind_ens true;`, updated source hashes, and no contract hash was accepted by `transform_pair` and emitted a record claiming the pinned contract hash.
findings.impact: The alternative adapter can produce a source candidate whose contract annotations differ from the pinned P2 contract while its stage record reports the pinned contract identity, breaking the source/contract pin invariant for later capture.
findings.fix: Require an explicit input contract hash and verify the exact expected contract bytes at their intended source boundary before transformation; derive the output hash only from bytes actually verified.

verified: smallsort-session review check matched exact candidate, spec, packet, and 15 packet files; packet proof_credit is NONE

The primary helper/owner/drop chain is Cloud-gated, uses the pinned provider module, rejects GitHub identity, and the owner-linked stage calls the mutable parallel fixture writer rather than the const fixture writer

Primary source adapters preserve ghost-stripped runtime bytes and label source certificates as generation-only; emitted records keep typed MIR binding false, proof NOT_RUN, admission absent, publication NOT_PUBLISHED, and proof credit zero
Per-component mutable rewrites in the owner-linked stage have expected counts 2/3/1 and reject wrong signature/depth patterns
17 synthetic tests passed across provider, primary source-chain, and alternate downstream adapters
A separate synthetic negative demonstrated acceptance of changed helper contract bytes when the input contract hash is omitted
not_run: Static request test suite: its setup calls the existing fixture writer against repository std source; skipped to honor the no-local-source-preparation boundary
Actual std source extraction/preparation, compiler/exporter/MIR decoder/refiner/verifier, Cloud, and proof runner
Any real proof or publication checks
limitations: This review establishes no Build result, typed MIR binding, translator admission, formal proof, publication, or proof credit.
